page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Electrical cables
lines: has a low density, so it is drawn into
wires and used for overhead power
steps.why: Aluminium is chosen for cables because good conductivity and low density come together in one metal, so the use and the reason for it fit in a single sentence.
common_mistakes: Naming a property instead of a use. Good conductivity is the reason; the cable is the use.
Giving a use of an aluminium compound, such as alum or aluminium oxide, when the question asks about the metal.
steps.memory_tip: Aluminium is light and conducts well, and that pair of properties is why cables are made of it.
steps.margin_note: One clear sentence names this use. A list of properties does not.

steps.label: Reducing agent in metallurgy
lines: Aluminium powder is a reducing agent in
metallurgy. In the thermite process it
reduces iron oxide to molten iron, which
is used to weld broken rails and machine
steps.why: Aluminium has a greater affinity for oxygen than iron has, so it removes the oxygen from iron oxide, and that one fact covers both the metallurgical use and the welding use.
common_mistakes: Writing the thermite equation unbalanced. Two aluminium atoms are needed for one Fe₂O₃.
Calling aluminium the oxidising agent here. It loses electrons, so it is the reducing agent.
steps.memory_tip: Aluminium has the greater affinity for oxygen, so it takes the oxygen and the other metal is left as molten metal.
steps.margin_note: Alloys for aircraft and vehicle parts, or foil for packing, are equally good second uses. The equation is extra.

insider_note: Two named uses, one sentence each, are the whole answer; a paragraph about aluminium's properties still names no use.
